1.explanation:
• src/ol/format/KML.js is the format implementation that reads the <name> element (and other text properties) via getAllTextContent/readString, and immediately hands that raw string—including any XML entities—to the style/Text pipeline without ever decoding entities. 

• src/ol/xml.js provides getAllTextContent (and parse) for the XML subsystem. Its text‐gathering routines must rely on node.innerHTML or manual child-node concatenation, so XML entities like ' are never converted back into their character equivalents. These two files need changes so that textContent (or an explicit entity decode step) is used, ensuring that “'” becomes “’” before styling or rendering occurs.
1.bug_scenario: When reading a KML placemark whose name contains XML character entities (e.g. “Andy's”), the entity is not being decoded before it’s passed through to the renderer. In the screenshot above you can see the feature label drawn literally as “Andy's Pub, Terrasse” and in the map tooltip underneath, rather than showing “Andy’s”, the apostrophe entity remains un‐decoded.
